originalTitle: Flock keeps ignoring requests to cancel its contracts

content: While more cities are canceling their contracts with Flock Safety, just as many are discovering how difficult that can be in some instances. Plymouth, Minnesota’s city council voted to terminate its contract with Flock in September, but failed to respond to the city’s request. For over a month, the cameras remained up, and the city had received no acknowledgment from the company. So, Police Chief Eric Fadden took matters into his own hands and physically disconnected the cameras. “After hearing nothing for more than a week, I directed our staff to disconnect the power cords from the cameras in order to be sure that they are not functioning or recording plates,” Fadden told The Drive. Roughly 20 miles up the road, Dayton, Minnesota, is having its own issues with Flock. In this instance, the company acknowledged the city’s request and said it would take up to 60 days to remove the equipment. Despite this, Flock reconnected two cameras within the city limits without authorization, and following a specific request from the local police not to complete the work order. Dayton’s local government posted on Facebook: > On September 17, 2026, the Police Department was made aware of a maintenance work order produced by Flock. The City notified Flock on September 18, 2026, that the program was on hold, and no work orders were to be completed. Unfortunately, the City’s direction was not followed, and the camera was placed back into service without authorization. Flock spokesperson Andrew Smith told The Verge, “We are proud of the impact our technology has had in Plymouth. We respect the city’s decision and are working with the customer to have the cameras removed.” This follows a similar ordeal in Illinois, where the company refused to take down cameras and uncovered cameras at Elgin Community College after the administration sought to cancel its contract. Update November 1st: Added comment from Flock.
chineseTitle: Flock 一直无视取消合同的请求
chineseSummary: 尽管越来越多的城市取消了与 Flock Safety 的合同，但许多城市也发现在某些情况下这可能是多么困难。明尼苏达州普利茅斯市议会9月份投票决定终止与Flock的合同，但未能回应该市的要求。一个多月以来，摄像机一直保持着状态，整个城市 […]
chineseContent: 尽管越来越多的城市取消了与 Flock Safety 的合同，但许多城市也发现在某些情况下这可能是多么困难。明尼苏达州普利茅斯市议会于 9 月投票决定终止与 Flock 的合同，但未能回应该市的要求。一个多月以来，摄像头一直处于开启状态，市政府没有收到该公司的任何回应。因此，警察局长埃里克·法登亲自处理此事并断开了摄像头的连接。 “在一个多星期没有听到任何消息后，我指示我们的工作人员拔掉摄像机的电源线，以确保它们无法正常工作或记录板，”法登告诉 The Drive。沿着这条路大约 20 英里，明尼苏达州代顿市也面临着弗洛克的问题。在这种情况下，该公司承认了市政府的要求，并表示最多需要 60 天的时间才能拆除这些设备。尽管如此，弗洛克未经授权在城市范围内重新连接了两台摄像机，并根据当地警方的具体要求不要完成工作指令。代顿当地政府在 Facebook 上发帖称： > 2026 年 9 月 17 日，警察局获悉 Flock 出具的一份维修工单。市政府于 2026 年 9 月 18 日通知 Flock，该计划已暂停，并且不会完成任何工单。不幸的是，市政府的指示并没有得到遵守，相机在未经授权的情况下又重新投入使用。 Flock 发言人安德鲁·史密斯 (Andrew Smith) 告诉 The Verge：“我们为我们的技术在普利茅斯产生的影响感到自豪。我们尊重该市的决定，并正在与客户合作拆除摄像头。”在此之前，伊利诺伊州也遭遇了类似的考验，该公司拒绝拆除埃尔吉的摄像头和裸露的摄像头
